raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`GigaChat3Detector.parse_streaming_increment` disagrees with `detect_and_parse`
in three ways, all reproducible on `main` by feeding one response in deltas of
different sizes. The non-streaming result is the reference for every case below.

**1. Protocol markers are printed as assistant text.** Content is derived from
the *delta* (`REGEX_CONTENT_PATTERN.search(delta_text)`), and when the delta holds
no complete marker the code falls back to `content = delta_text`. A marker that
straddles a delta boundary is therefore emitted verbatim:

```
input   : <|message_sep|>\n\nfunction call<|role_sep|>\n{"name": "manage_user_memory", ...}
streamed: "<|message_sep|>\n\nfunction call<|role_sep|>\n"     <- shown to the user
expected: ""
```

Reproduces at 1, 5 and 13 characters per delta, i.e. for most real framings; only
a delta large enough to contain the whole marker avoided it.

**2. The arguments can arrive as invalid JSON.** The end token is stripped only
when it is complete (`if cur_args.endswith("</s>")`), so an intermediate snapshot
that ends mid-token is emitted as an argument delta. No later delta can repair a
string the client has already concatenated, so the accumulated arguments stay
broken -- which is also why the detector logs its own
`Arguments overlap mismatch` warning:

```
streamed arguments: '{"action": "create", "id": "test"}}</s'   <- not JSON
expected          : '{"action": "create", "id": "test"}'
```

**3. A call completing inside one delta loses its arguments.** The parser sends
the tool name first and the arguments on a later call; there was no `finish()`
override, so with a single delta the client received the call with empty
arguments:

```
input   : <|function_call|>{"name": "manage_user_memory", "arguments": {...}}
streamed: [(0, "manage_user_memory", "")]      (at 145 chars per delta: no call at all)
expected: [(0, "manage_user_memory", '{"action": "create", "id": "preferences"}')]
```

All three are reachable whenever a call completes inside a single delta
(multi-token deltas from speculative decoding / MTP, `stream_interval > 1`) or
whenever a marker is split across deltas, which is the normal case for
character-level streaming.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/function_call/gigachat3_detector.py` (+82/-9):

- **Content comes from the accumulated buffer**, like `detect_and_parse`, and only
  the part before the marker is emitted. A suffix that could still become a marker
  is held until it is decided, and the already-emitted length is tracked so text
  is sent exactly once.
- **A partial end token is held back** instead of being emitted as arguments, so
  the streamed argument string stays a prefix of the cleaned value.
- **`finish()`** drains pending state by re-running the parser with an empty delta
  until a round yields neither calls nor text, following the pattern
  `GigaChat35Detector.finish()` already uses. The empty-delta early return now
  also processes a non-empty buffer, which is what makes the drain possible.

`test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py` (+99): three
cases in `TestGigaChat3Detector`, all three failing on `main`, parametrized over
chunk sizes 1, 5, 13, 16, 24, 32, 48 and whole-response.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A -- parser-only change, no model forward or kernel code touched.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A -- the added work is bounded by the number of pending units at end of stream.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean; the detector
      has zero findings and the test file keeps its 6 pre-existing `F841`.
- [x] Add unit tests per the repo's admission criteria (bug regression: all three
      fail before the change and pass after it).
- [x] Duplicate pre-check: searched open PRs on
      `python/sglang/srt/function_call/gigachat3_detector.py` -- none.
- [ ] Documentation: N/A

### Verification

```
pytest test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py
# 253 passed, 51 subtests passed            (250 before this change)

pytest ... -k "protocol_markers or split_end_token or releases_arguments_of_a_call"
# with the fix:     3 passed
# detector reverted: 3 failed

pytest test/registered/unit/function_call test/registered/unit/parser
# 1061 passed, 1793 subtests passed
```

Framing sweep over the five inputs from the audit, at every chunk size from 1 to
the full response: **58 of 58 checks now match the non-streaming result** (text
and accumulated arguments); on `main` 30 of them diverged.

---

Disclosure: prepared with AI assistance (DeepSeek Harness). The reproduction, the
pre-fix failures and the post-fix passes were all executed locally on CPU with
`PYTHONPATH` at the checkout.

<!-- pr-states:start -->
---
### CI States

Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #38027023453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38027023453)<!-- slot:pr-test:end -->
Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #38027023228](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38027023228)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end -->
Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd:start -->:x: [Run #38027023440](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38027023440)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd:end -->
<!-- pr-states:end -->

---

**Reviewer note — why the drain sits in `finish()` and not in the base class.**

There is an open base-class fix for part of this defect class (#32167, "Fix streaming tool calls losing arguments when completed in the final delta"). It does not cover this detector, and the reason is worth recording before anyone has to ask:

- The shared flush path is `FunctionCallParser.parse_stream_end()` -> `detector.finish()`, and **both** streaming entrypoints call it (`serving_chat.py:3030`, `serving_responses.py:2399`). The flush that #32167 extends, `_check_for_unstreamed_tool_args`, exists only in `serving_chat.py` (defined at 3115, used at 945); `serving_responses.py` has no equivalent.
- `BaseFormatDetector.parse_streaming_increment` processes exactly **one** JSON object per call — there is no loop between the `bot_token` search and the Case 1 / Case 2 returns. A delta carrying several complete calls therefore leaves the rest buffered, and registering the single object that was parsed does not recover them; the drain here re-runs the parser until it yields nothing, which does.
- `GigaChat3Detector.parse_streaming_increment` is a fully custom state machine that never calls `super()`, so a base-class registration cannot reach it at all. This detector also differs in kind: the defects fixed here are protocol markers leaking into `content` and invalid-JSON argument tails (`...}}</s`), not only a lost final-delta call.

---

**Duplicate check (required before writing code).**

Searched open and draft PRs by file path, class name and defect description. The
closest competitor is **#32167** ("Fix streaming tool calls losing arguments when
completed in the final delta"), which patches the shared `BaseFormatDetector`; the
reason this detector-level fix is not subsumed by it is in the reviewer note above
(`GigaChat3Detector.parse_streaming_increment` never delegates to `super()`, and the
base parses one object per increment without draining the buffer).

Adjacent but distinct PRs touching the same shared test file — #28845 (Llama32
truncating text after the final call), #29582 (single quotes inside JSON values in
Llama32 streaming), #40291/#40295 (LFM2), #40741 (qwen3_coder) — address different
defects in different detectors; none of them drains a detector's pending calls at
stream end.

### Residual: the "arguments overlap mismatch" guard is kept, deliberately

The readiness pass flagged `gigachat3_detector.py:207-212` — the `else` branch that logs
`Arguments overlap mismatch` and returns an empty result — as a branch no input reaches.
Read against the code, it has no reachable input, and I am nevertheless keeping it, which
is a change from how the sibling residual in `qwen25_detector.py` was resolved.

Why it is unreachable: `cur_args` is `ARGS_REGEX.group(1).strip()` taken from the
*accumulated* buffer (`self._buffer += new_text`), and `ARGS_REGEX` is
`'"arguments"\s*:\s*(.*)'` with `re.DOTALL` — a greedy capture to the end of the buffer. The buffer only ever grows, so the
capture only ever extends; the two things that can shorten it are removing a trailing
`</s>` and dropping a trailing `}` when what remains still parses as JSON, and both remove
a suffix rather than mutating the middle. The prefix relation the guard tests therefore
holds by construction, and nine synthetic stream shapes in the earlier round failed to
break it, which is consistent.

Why keep it rather than delete it: the two options are not behaviourally symmetric, which
they were for the `qwen25` case. There the removed line simply never executed, so deleting
it changed nothing. Here, if the branch is ever reached and the guard is gone, control
falls through to `delta_args = cur_args[len(prev_args):]` on a string that is *not* an
extension of `prev_args` — sending the client a nonsense slice of the arguments instead of
a refused one. A cheap refusal plus a warning is the better failure mode for an invariant
this load-bearing, so the branch stays as a defensive assertion of the invariant.

The consequence to be honest about: it remains uncovered by the suite, so it reads as dead
code to a coverage report. Anyone who later wants it gone should first change the fallback
to something safe rather than removing the check outright.

- The duplicate pre-check is recorded in the PR body: I searched open PRs on
  `gigachat3_detector.py` and found none. Separately I noticed #35625 targets

  bug; this change is scoped to GigaChat3 and does not touch shared code.
- The `finish()` drain relies on the empty-delta guard now processing a non-empty

_Posting these numbers for the record. The runs were executed with AI assistance
(DeepSeek Harness), consistent with the disclosure in the PR description._

Note on the `Recommend tests from coverage` check, which is red on this head.

It is not related to this diff, and the job is advisory by construction:
`pr-test-npu.yml` marks it `continue-on-error: true` with the comment "so it never
blocks the PR gate". It failed inside the PR-diff fetch:

```
Fetching changes from GitHub PR: sgl-project/sglang#41034
  Attempt 1/3 to get PR diff via GitHub API...
  Attempt 1 failed: HTTP Error 503: Service Unavailable
  Attempt 2/3 ... HTTP Error 503
  Attempt 3/3 ... HTTP Error 503
  All 3 attempts failed, exiting
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

The same failure mode appears at the same time on the docs-only #41046 and on my
#41052, and 6 of 25 open PRs sampled at that moment carry the same failing
conclusion -- so it tracks the API, not any particular change. It appears
transient; a re-run of the job should clear it (I have no write access to
re-trigger workflows).

The underlying gap is small: `scripts/ci/npu/precise-test/test_selector.py`
retries three times at a flat 1 s spacing and then `exit(1)`s, which is a ~2 s
window against a GitHub 503, and it turns an advisory job red. I have a prepared
two-line fix -- exponential backoff matching the house pattern in
`scripts/ci/utils/publish_traces.py`, and not failing an advisory job -- and can
open it separately if that is useful. Flagging it here only so the red check is not
mistaken for a problem in this PR.

files.patch:
@@ -34,6 +34,16 @@
 )
 
 
+END_TOKEN = "</s>"
+MARKER_FUNCTION_CALL = "function call<|role_sep|>\n"
+MARKER_FUNCTION_CALL_INLINE = "<|function_call|>"
+MARKER_MESSAGE_SEP = "<|message_sep|>"
+
+# Upper bound for the end-of-stream drain: each round releases at most one pending
+# unit (a tool name or one argument diff).
+_MAX_FINISH_DRAIN_ROUNDS = 1024
+
+
 class GigaChat3Detector(BaseFormatDetector):
     def __init__(self) -> None:
         super().__init__()
@@ -42,6 +52,10 @@ def __init__(self) -> None:
         self.end_content: bool = False
         self._buffer: str = ""
         self.prev_tool_call_arr: list[dict] = []
+        # Length of the assistant text already streamed, so the pre-marker
+        # portion is emitted exactly once even when the marker is split across
+        # deltas.
+        self._content_sent: int = 0
 
     def has_tool_call(self, text: str) -> bool:
         """Check if text contains a tool call marker"""
@@ -102,24 +116,41 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
         Streaming parser for incremental text chunks.
         Maintains state across calls to build complete tool calls.
         """
-        if not new_text:
+        if not new_text and not self._buffer:
+            # Keep processing an empty delta while something is buffered: this is
+            # what lets finish() release state the last delta left pending.
             return StreamingParseResult()
         logger.debug(f"[GigaChat3] parse_streaming_increment: '{new_text}'")
         self._buffer += new_text
         current_text = self._buffer
-        delta_text = new_text
         content = None
         func_name = None
         cur_args = None
         m_func = REGEX_FUNCTION_CALL.search(current_text)
         if not self.tool_started:
-            m_content = REGEX_CONTENT_PATTERN.search(delta_text)
+            # Derive the visible text from the accumulated buffer rather than
+            # from this delta: a marker can straddle a delta boundary, and
+            # emitting the delta verbatim would print the protocol tokens
+            # themselves ("<|message_sep|>function call<|role_sep|>") to the
+            # user. Only the portion before the marker is content, and a suffix
+            # that could still become a marker is held until it is decided.
+            m_content = REGEX_CONTENT_PATTERN.search(current_text)
             if m_content:
-                content = m_content.group(1)
+                before_marker = m_content.group(1)
+                content = before_marker[self._content_sent :]
+                self._content_sent = len(before_marker)
                 self.end_content = True
-            else:
-                if not self.end_content:
-                    content = delta_text
+            elif not self.end_content:
+                held = max(
+                    self._ends_with_partial_token(current_text, MARKER_FUNCTION_CALL),
+                    self._ends_with_partial_token(
+                        current_text, MARKER_FUNCTION_CALL_INLINE
+                    ),
+                    self._ends_with_partial_token(current_text, MARKER_MESSAGE_SEP),
+                )
+                safe_end = len(current_text) - held if held else len(current_text)
+                content = current_text[self._content_sent : safe_end]
+                self._content_sent = safe_end
             if m_func:
                 self.tool_started = True
                 logger.debug("[GigaChat3] Tool call started")
@@ -134,8 +165,14 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
         args_match = ARGS_REGEX.search(json_tail)
         if args_match:
             cur_args = args_match.group(1).strip()
-            if cur_args.endswith("</s>"):
-                cur_args = cur_args[: -len("</s>")]
+            if cur_args.endswith(END_TOKEN):
+                cur_args = cur_args[: -len(END_TOKEN)]
+            elif self._ends_with_partial_token(cur_args, END_TOKEN):
+                # The end token is still arriving. Emitting now would send an
+                # argument prefix that includes part of "</s>" (and possibly the
+                # outer closing brace), and no later delta can repair a string
+                # the client has already concatenated, so wait for it.
+                return StreamingParseResult()
             if cur_args.endswith("}"):
                 try:
                     candidate = cur_args[:-1].strip()
@@ -191,6 +228,29 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
         )
         return StreamingParseResult(calls=calls)
 
+    def finish(self, tools: List[Tool]) -> StreamingParseResult:
+        """Release tool-call state the last delta left pending.
+
+        parse_streaming_increment emits the tool name first and its arguments on
+        a later call. When the delta that completes the call is the last one
+        (multi-token deltas from speculative decoding / MTP,
+        ``stream_interval > 1``, or a call short enough to be generated in one
+        step) nothing picks the arguments up, so the client received the call
+        with empty arguments or, for a call still incomplete, no call at all --
+        while detect_and_parse returned it in full.
+
+        Re-running the parser with an empty delta drains that queue. Only calls
+        can be pending: this detector emits content as it arrives and keeps no
+        text back waiting for a marker, so nothing else has to be released.
+        """
+        calls: List[ToolCallItem] = []
+        for _ in range(_MAX_FINISH_DRAIN_ROUNDS):
+            result = self.parse_streaming_increment("", tools)
+            if not result.calls:
+                break
+            calls.extend(result.calls)

+        detector = GigaChat3Detector()

+                store[call.tool_index][0] = call.name
+            store[call.tool_index][1] += call.parameters or ""

### Author verification

Re-ran on the branch head `bb44824daa` (minutes before posting this):

```
pytest test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py
# 253 passed, 51 subtests passed          (250 before this change)

pytest ... -k "protocol_markers or split_end_token or releases_arguments_of_a_call"
# with the fix:      3 passed
# detector reverted: 3 failed

pytest test/registered/unit/function_call test/registered/unit/parser
# 1061 passed, 1793 subtests passed
```

Framing sweep over the five inputs from the audit, at every chunk size from 1 to
the whole response, comparing against `detect_and_parse`:

```
before: 30 divergences - markup in the visible text at 1/5/13 per delta,
        arguments ending '...}}</s' (invalid JSON), empty arguments or no call
        at large framings
after : 58 of 58 checks match (text and accumulated arguments)
```

Two notes that may be useful when reviewing:

- The duplicate pre-check is recorded in the PR body: I searched open PRs on
  `gigachat3_detector.py` and found none. Separately I noticed #35625 targets
  several other detectors for the same streaming/non-streaming parity class of
  bug; this change is scoped to GigaChat3 and does not touch shared code.
- The `finish()` drain relies on the empty-delta guard now processing a non-empty
  buffer. Before, `parse_streaming_increment("")` returned immediately, so no
  drain was possible for this detector without that change.

Environment: the CPU venv with `PYTHONPATH` pointed at the checkout.

_Posting these numbers for the record. The runs were executed with AI assistance
(DeepSeek Harness), consistent with the disclosure in the PR description._

Note on the `Recommend tests from coverage` check, which is red on this head.

It is not related to this diff, and the job is advisory by construction:
`pr-test-npu.yml` marks it `continue-on-error: true` with the comment "so it never
blocks the PR gate". It failed inside the PR-diff fetch:

```
Fetching changes from GitHub PR: sgl-project/sglang#41034
  Attempt 1/3 to get PR diff via GitHub API...
  Attempt 1 failed: HTTP Error 503: Service Unavailable
  Attempt 2/3 ... HTTP Error 503
  Attempt 3/3 ... HTTP Error 503
  All 3 attempts failed, exiting
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

The same failure mode appears at the same time on the docs-only #41046 and on my
#41052, and 6 of 25 open PRs sampled at that moment carry the same failing
conclusion -- so it tracks the API, not any particular change. It appears
transient; a re-run of the job should clear it (I have no write access to
re-trigger workflows).

The underlying gap is small: `scripts/ci/npu/precise-test/test_selector.py`
retries three times at a flat 1 s spacing and then `exit(1)`s, which is a ~2 s
window against a GitHub 503, and it turns an advisory job red. I have a prepared
two-line fix -- exponential backoff matching the house pattern in
`scripts/ci/utils/publish_traces.py`, and not failing an advisory job -- and can
open it separately if that is useful. Flagging it here only so the red check is not
mistaken for a problem in this PR.
